result.topic_en: Ramanujan gives bounds and an asymptotic formula for sigma_{-s}(N), then defines generalised highly composite and generalised superior highly composite numbers with respect to sigma_{-s}, stating the required form of their prime factorisation.

59. {+A number+} N may be said to be a generalised highly composite num-
ber if $\sigma_{-s}(N) > \sigma_{-s}(N')$ for all values of $N'$ less than N. We can
easily show that, in order that N should be a generalised high
-ly composite number, N must be of the form
(303) $2^{a_2}\, 3^{a_3}\, 5^{a_5} \cdots\cdots p^{a_p}$,
where $a_2 \geq a_3 \geq a_5 \geq \cdots\cdots \geq a_p = 1$,
the exceptional numbers being 36, for the values of s which satis

A number N may be said to be a generalised supe-
rior highly composite number if there is a positive number
$\epsilon$ such that
(304) $\frac{\sigma_{-s}(N)}{N^{\epsilon}} \geq \frac{\sigma_{-s}(N')}{(N')^{\epsilon}}$,
for all values of $N'$ less than N, and
(305) $\frac{\sigma_{-s}(N)}{N^{\epsilon}} > \frac{\sigma_{-s}(N')}{(N')^{\epsilon}}$
for all values of $N'$ greater than N. It is easily seen that
all generalised superior highly composite numbers are also
